text:
eng-oncall-bot: pager: P0 - spike in 5xx for /v1/generate in prod-us-east-1 (alert: rollout_high_error_rate). Oncall: amanda

amanda (oncall): On it, pulling logs and dashboards now.

robin (sre): Seeing 503/502s from inference-worker canary. readinessProbe failures + CrashLoopBackOff on a subset of pods.

nick (infra): HPA jumped from 3 -> 12 in the last 4m for that deployment, CPU on encoder nodes hit 95%. Could be autoscaler overreaction to probe failures.

raj (pm): We rolled the new-health-check flag and canary image 3.2.4-canary-2 ~10m ago. Can someone confirm if that changed probes?

robin (sre): deploy/inference-worker uses image=redwood/inference:3.2.4-canary-2. readinessProbe: exec curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1; periodSeconds: 5; failureThreshold: 1 — that's very aggressive for this process.

carla (customer-ops): Customers reporting timeouts and retries. Outreach drafting a holding message. No confirmed errors to user data, mostly transient errors.

amanda (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) Pause traffic to canary, 2) Rollback to 3.2.3, 3) If rollback stalls flip feature flag new-health-check off, 4) Triage HPA scaling.

robin (sre): Pausing canary routing now (/control/rollout pause) — done. Attempting rollback to 3.2.3.

eng-oncall-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated for deploy/inference-worker -> image:3.2.3 by @robin

robin (sre): Executing: kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-worker --to-revision=3

nick (infra): FYI node drain was kicked in us-east-1a for maintenance, some pods received SIGTERM and exited before clean shutdown. terminationGracePeriodSeconds might be too short for this workload.

amanda (oncall): Rollback reports: 6/8 pods rolled back successfully, 2 stuck CrashLoopBackOff. Investigating stuck ones.

robin (sre): Forcing delete of stuck pods to trigger new replicas from 3.2.3: kubectl delete pod inference-worker-xyz -n prod

nick (infra): Deleted stuck pods; new pods launching on 3.2.3. Also lowered HPA max from 15 -> 6 to reduce churn while stabilizing.

eng-oncall-bot: alert: 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 2% over last 5m

carla (customer-ops): Customer ops sent initial bulletin: impact = degraded performance for some requests; mitigation in progress; no confirmed data loss.

raj (pm): Can we flip the new-health-check flag off as extra precaution?

amanda (oncall): Flipped new-health-check=false via feature-proxy :white_check_mark:

robin (sre): Readiness failures stopping. Initiating rolling restart of remaining pods to ensure stable image roll.

eng-oncall-bot: tag: incident/5187654321-rollout-healthcheck-regression created for tracking

amanda (oncall): Handoff: @sre-liz for overnight monitoring. TL;DR: rolled back to 3.2.3, feature flag off, HPA scaled down, keep an eye on pod restart frequency and error rate.

sre-liz: Acknowledged. Will watch error rate, pod restarts, and HPA activity through the night.

carla (customer-ops): Follow-up sent to affected customers with timeline and mitigation steps. No SLA breach currently; monitoring continues.

robin (sre): Action items for postmortem: - Relax readinessProbe (failureThreshold: 3, periodSeconds: 10), add startupProbe for slow init, increase terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 60, add canary traffic shaping to avoid HPA overreaction, add k8s e2e for probe behaviour.

amanda (oncall): Assigning postmortem owner: @raj. Draft RCA due EOD tomorrow. Preliminary root cause: aggressive readinessProbe introduced by flag + HPA surge + node drain SIGTERM race leading to pod churn and elevated 5xx.

eng-oncall-bot: closing page: error rate normalized <1% for 15m — incident moved to monitoring

robin (sre): Leaving a note: if anyone sees a repeat spike, escalate immediately and consider emergency kill-switch for rollout service routes.
